Probing `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][4]` in this early-round window exposes an internal representation before all 24 rounds have diffused the input. The implementation carries the effect through `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.e[0][4] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][4]`. The observation leaks lane-level information about the secret input that is not present as a directly accessible architectural signal.

On subsequent `calc` cycles, feedback from the registered permutation output re-enters the same combinational round network. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][4]` is recomputed for later round pairs and therefore yields a time series of input-dependent values from a nonlinear chi result lane. Sampling `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][4]` at a fixed cycle offset across repeated operations supplies aligned intermediate values for differential or correlation analysis. The implementation carries the effect through `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.e[0][4] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.f[0][4]`. Combining those observations can recover secret-dependent relationships even when a single lane observation is insufficient to reconstruct the input.
